summary: Defines a new SIP header field, Feature-Caps, which carries feature-capability indicators showing support for features and capabilities of SIP entities not identified by the URI of the Contact header field. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: It is a name tag listing what each helper in a phone call can do, so others know what to ask for.

questions: what is the sip feature-caps header
how to indicate sip capabilities of proxies
how do sip proxies indicate supported features
what are the g. and sip. feature-capability trees
subtitle: A SIP header that lets proxies, registrars and B2BUAs advertise what they support.

tldr.problem: SIP user agents can announce features with media feature tags in the Contact header field, but proxies, registrars and some B2BUAs are not represented by the Contact URI and so had no way to do the same.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6809 defines the Feature-Caps header field, which carries feature-capability indicators, and creates an IANA registry with a global tree (g.) and a SIP tree (sip.) for registering them.
tldr.outcome: Entities on the signaling path can now announce supported features, while each individual indicator's specification defines how the feature is used. The RFC is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 6809 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, and the RFC itself registers no initial indicators in either tree.

sections.title: Why Another Capability Header
sections.content:
The SIP extension in RFC 3840 lets a message carry information about the originator's features and capabilities in the Contact header field. That only works for an entity represented by the Contact URI.

RFC 6809 adds a header field, Feature-Caps, for entities that are not represented that way. The RFC lists three cases: the entity acts as a SIP proxy, it acts as a SIP registrar, or it acts as a Back-to-Back User Agent (B2BUA) where the Contact URI represents another entity. The values it carries are called feature-capability indicators. Unlike media feature tags, they are intended to be used only with SIP.
sections.plainLanguage: Some helpers in a phone call do not have their own name tag. This gives them a way to wear a tag listing what they can do.

sections.title: How Entities Use Feature-Caps
sections.content:
A feature-capability indicator in a Feature-Caps header field says that some entity in the SIP message signaling path supports the associated feature. An entity whose own URI is in the Contact header field MUST NOT use Feature-Caps for its support. The header field cannot carry the address of the entity that inserted it. If that address matters, the feature's own definition has to put it in an indicator value.

A proxy that wants to advertise support towards downstream entities inserts the header in the request before forwarding. To advertise towards upstream entities, it inserts it in the response. A B2BUA that is referenced by a Record-Route header field does the same, and MAY also copy received Feature-Caps fields, like a proxy. A registrar inserts the header in a REGISTER response.

An entity that adds a Feature-Caps header field MUST place it before any existing one, so the top-most one is the closest from a signaling point of view. Entities MAY remove a whole header field or single indicators, and SHOULD NOT re-order the header fields. Order within one field has no significance, so foo;bar and bar;foo mean the same.
sections.plainLanguage: Each helper adds its tag to the top of the pile as a message passes through, so the helper nearest to you is always on top.

sections.title: Dialogs, Registrations and Standalone Requests
sections.content:
How long an indicator applies depends on the message type. In a dialog, the header can appear in an initial request, a target refresh request and any 18x or 2xx response to them. An indicator in an initial request applies for the dialog until a target refresh request is sent or the dialog ends. If a later target refresh request or its response lacks the indicator, the feature is no longer supported for the dialog. An entity MUST insert the same indicators in all 18x and 2xx responses of one transaction. For SUBSCRIBE, forking means the 2xx may not reach the UAC, so support is indicated in the NOTIFY sent for each subscription dialog.

For REGISTER, the header can appear in the request and in the 200 (OK) response. Support lasts until the explicitly registered contact expires, or until a refresh REGISTER omits the indicator, and applies only to contacts conveyed in that request. Pure binding-fetch REGISTERs, with no Contact header field, MUST NOT carry the header. With SIP outbound (RFC 5626), support applies only to the flow on which it was indicated.

In a standalone request, an indicator applies for the duration of that transaction.
sections.plainLanguage: A tag is only good for as long as the conversation it was attached to. If the next message does not repeat it, the helper no longer promises that skill.

sections.title: Syntax of the Header and Indicators
sections.content:
The ABNF follows RFC 5234. The header field is Feature-Caps followed by one or more fc-value items separated by commas. Each fc-value starts with an asterisk, then any number of semicolon-separated feature-capability indicators. The asterisk is there to follow the syntax guidelines of RFC 4485 and to stay consistent with RFCs 3840 and 3841.

Each indicator starts with a mandatory +, then a name, and optionally an equals sign and a quoted value list or string value. Unlike media feature tags, the + is always required. Dots in a name can build a tree hierarchy such as tree.feature.subfeature, and its use must be described at registration.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a form with fixed boxes. Each skill gets a plus sign and a name, and may have a quoted detail after it.

sections.title: Defining and Registering Indicators
sections.content:
The RFC creates the IANA sub-registry "Proxy-Feature Feature-Capability Indicator Trees". Indicators are sorted into trees by their leading facet, the prefix up to and including the first dot. The RFC defines two trees. The global tree uses the leading facet g. and needs "Specification Required" with a designated expert. The SIP tree uses sip. and needs "IETF Review". Names with no dot have an empty leading facet and have no tree. No initial values are registered in either tree, and no leading + is used in registrations.

An indicator's own specification MUST cover an overall description, values and their syntax, usage restrictions, interoperability considerations and security considerations, and it is recommended to include examples. It MUST NOT change the Feature-Caps rules in this RFC or weaken any SHOULD or MUST, though it MAY strengthen a SHOULD, MAY or RECOMMENDED to MUST. The registration template asks for the name, a description of no more than 4 lines, the specification reference and a contact.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two official lists where new skill names can be filed, one easier to get into and one run by the standards group, and every new skill has to come with its own instructions.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The end-user privacy concerns of RFC 3840 do not apply, because these indicators are not meant to describe end-user devices, and the caller-preferences routing concern does not apply because the mechanism is not defined for use with indicators.

Indicators can still reveal sensitive details about SIP entities. Malicious elements that see them may learn deployment details or spot elements with exploitable weaknesses. The header does not carry addresses, but individual indicator values might. If an indicator needs integrity or origin authentication, its specification MUST provide mechanisms for it. If it needs confidentiality, the specification MUST call for TLS at all hops, and specifications SHOULD NOT define indicators that need better confidentiality than hop-by-hop TLS gives.
sections.plainLanguage: A skill list can give away secrets about a helper, so anything private should only be sent over a locked connection.

data.title: Feature-Caps and feature-capability indicator
data.code:
Feature-Caps = "Feature-Caps" HCOLON fc-value
                *(COMMA fc-value)
fc-value     = "*" *(SEMI feature-cap)

feature-cap       =  "+" fcap-name [EQUAL LDQUOT (fcap-value-list
                         / fcap-string-value ) RDQUOT]
fcap-name         =  ftag-name
fcap-value-list   =  tag-value-list
fcap-string-value =  string-value
